title: MemoryStand — presenter cut
presenterDisclosure: Presenter synthesised from the author's own photograph.
_notes: Six beats at 15s. Under the 3:00 hackathon ceiling with room to spare, and short enough
that a judge finishes it. The evidence-deck cut (docs/demo/video-timeline.json) stays in
the repo as the long-form artifact; this is the submission video.
Every number spoken here is measured and traceable:
beat 4 recall   -> live /decide response, README quotes it verbatim
beat 5 refusal  -> live /confirm_outcome, 400 with the CloudWatch delta
beat 6 prior art-> README 'Prior art, stated honestly'
Word counts are sized for ~145 wpm, which is the rate the narration renders at. A 15s
beat is ~36 words; going over means the clip runs past its own panel animation.

beats.speech: Every shipping agent-memory system asks a model whether its own memory is true. Mem0, Zep, AWS AgentCore. MemoryStand asks CloudWatch instead — and refuses the promotion when CloudWatch disagrees.

lines: Mem0 — an LLM picks ADD/UPDATE/DELETE. No confidence score at all.
Zep — an LLM sets validity windows. "Model-inferred, not authoritative."
AWS AgentCore — extraction and consolidation are LLM prompts. No verification API.
panelData.footnote: Each line cites the vendor's own docs or issue tracker. See README.

beats.speech: The failure isn't fraud. It's an engineer at two in the morning who restarts a service, watches the page clear, and reports in good faith that the restart fixed it — when the metric never moved.

panelData.headline: Nobody lied. The memory is still false.
panelData.body: And it will be handed to an agent at the next incident. That is how a memory store fills with true-sounding operational folklore.

beats.speech: So we measured it. Six hundred poisoned claims, plus honest ones as a control. Trusting the caller admits every attack. An LLM judge blocks every attack — and every honest claim too.

panelData.footnote: benchmarks/poisoning.md · judge arm run live, not estimated

beats.speech: A defence that refuses all evidence stops all poisoning, and is useless. Only the outcome gate tells the two apart — and it does it with zero model calls on the promotion path.

panelData.label: model calls on the promotion path
panelData.body: backend/trust.py imports no model client, and a runtime guard fails if one becomes reachable even one import away.

beats.speech: Here it is deciding. Two candidate memories: the nearer one is unconfirmed, the further one was checked against CloudWatch. Proximity said one thing. Trust said another. Trust won.
None of this is a new idea. Doyle's truth maintenance systems retracted beliefs in 1979. What's unusual is a 2026 memory system that won't let a model grade its own memory — and enforces it.

lines: Doyle, JTMS, 1979 — a belief holds only while its justification does
CHEF, 1986 — cases retained by whether the plan actually worked
